resources.string: Local-first · Auditable · Continuous Mac × Android link
Pair first. Optional permissions stay off until you choose them.
Your phone connects directly to your Mac over LAN TLS. There is no account, cloud relay, or default telemetry.
Show the pairing QR on the Mac. If your camera recognizes custom links, tap the hyphen://pair result to return here. Camera support varies by device.
Paste the complete pairing link, or the address and nonce shown by the Mac. Both paths use the same strict parser.
Trust only if the six-digit code is identical on the phone and Mac. Both devices must confirm before trust is saved.
After pairing, notification mirroring and the persistent companion link remain optional. Each explains its access before opening Android settings or showing a foreground notification.
Restart the authenticated LAN session now instead of waiting for the current link to recover.
Skip the pending backoff and try the current trusted Mac again now.
Retry the saved, fingerprint-pinned route. If the route is unavailable, Hyphen will ask you to pair again.
The trusted Mac no longer has a usable local route on this phone. Open the Mac pairing screen and pair again.
Android restarted Hyphen while pairing was active. Scan or paste the current pairing code again; Hyphen will not guess which earlier link was in progress.
Hyphen could not open a system camera app. Paste the pairing link or address from the Mac instead; Hyphen does not request camera access.

Code: %1$s\n\nTrust this Mac only if it shows the same code.

Hyphen can read Android notification titles, actions, and content so it can mirror them to your paired Mac over local TLS.

Notifications are not sent to a cloud relay, and Hyphen does not store notification history. You can switch to hidden-body mode after enabling if you want less detail on the Mac.

Hyphen never asks for SMS or Call Log access. You can turn notification access off later in Android Settings.

Beta diagnostics are off by default.

Turn them on only while troubleshooting a beta issue. Local previews and exports may include trace IDs used to correlate failures; notification bodies, filenames, URLs, and IP suffixes stay redacted.

Hyphen never uploads diagnostics automatically. Exports are always user-initiated, and you can turn this off at any time.
Shows the local paired-Mac link and user-initiated transfers.

The platform time limit was reached. Open Hyphen and reselect the file to retry.
The foreground-service notification stays visible; disconnect any time.
Background continuity starts only when you explicitly enable it.
Scan the Mac\'s Hyphen QR with the system camera; its pairing link returns here for validation.
Scan the QR code on your Mac

1. Open “Pair new device” from the Hyphen menu on your Mac.
2. Scan its QR code with the Android system camera.
3. Open the hyphen://pair link to return here.
4. Trust only when both devices show the same pairing code.

This path does not give Hyphen camera access or add a third-party scanner SDK.

Hyphen will run a connectedDevice foreground service with an always-visible notification. It communicates only with the paired Mac over LAN TLS—no cloud relay or telemetry. Disconnect any time from the notification or this screen.
The background companion link can only connect to a Mac already verified by QR or SAS. Complete pairing first.
For transparency, Hyphen will not keep a background link when its notification is hidden. Allow Hyphen notifications in system settings, then try again.
This LAN discovery window found nothing. You can still scan the pairing QR with the system camera, or paste the address and nonce shown on the Mac pairing screen.
%1$s\n\nDiscovery results are LAN hints, not trust credentials. Open Hyphen\'s pairing screen on one of these Macs and scan its QR code.

Choosing a file temporarily leaves Hyphen. To avoid a hidden background link, Hyphen first enables the visible companion-link notification and shows a dataSync notification while sending. The companion link stays on until you disconnect from the notification or this screen.
The Mac may choose a stricter mode for an app, but it cannot loosen this setting. Notification history is not stored.
